subject: Andrii Andriichuk
profile_purpose: Realistic professional collaboration profile to set expectations, assess fit and potential, and anticipate friction. Not a marketing bio.

nodes.label: Openness and transparency
nodes.description: Explicitly communicate problems and risks early.

nodes.label: Constructive positivity
nodes.description: Keep a positive, constructive spirit unless human life or health is at stake.

nodes.label: Solution and future orientation
nodes.description: Focus on solutions and future perspectives rather than blame.

nodes.label: Explicit decisions and observability
nodes.description: Document known trade-offs and reasoning to prevent future assumptions.

nodes.label: Kindness and learning
nodes.description: Value people despite mistakes and turn failures into lessons, e.g. blameless postmortems.

nodes.label: Evidence over unsupported opinion
nodes.description: Prefer facts, measurements, and reasoned arguments.

nodes.label: Serving many people
nodes.description: Providing value to as many people as possible, directly or indirectly, is the main source of purpose and fulfilment at work.

nodes.label: Respect and supportive attitude
nodes.description: Respect for everyone regardless of age, gender, or background; a supportive attitude as a cross-cutting concept.

nodes.label: End customers first
nodes.description: Customer value and experience are the top priority; internal problems should not be pushed onto customers.

nodes.label: Stakeholders and colleagues second
nodes.description: Important collaborators, after end-customer priorities.

nodes.label: Quality serves value
nodes.description: Engineering quality matters, but as a means to create value, not an absolute end. Trade-offs are acceptable when explicit.

nodes.label: Explicit decision ownership
nodes.description: Voice implications and document the trade-off, rationale, and decision owner; leave business trade-off decisions to the appropriate owner.

nodes.label: Metrics steer direction
nodes.description: Good observability and sufficient KPIs should show outcomes and guide direction. Without measurement, results remain questionable.

nodes.label: Strongly scoped focus
nodes.description: Real expertise needs a scoped area; one person cannot be an expert across the whole 'fullstack' or 'DevSecOps' landscape.

nodes.label: Legal compliance and clear security issues
nodes.description: Legal non-compliance and clear security issues are no-go areas; risk assessment can be uncertain.

nodes.label: Respect agreed rules
nodes.description: Rules can be re-evaluated, but should be respected by everyone until formally changed.

nodes.label: Ethical project exclusions
nodes.description: Will not work on cryptocurrencies, mass surveillance, people manipulation, or illegal or gray-area projects.

nodes.label: Work stays out of the personal sphere
nodes.description: Work should not influence personal life, health, religion, or political preferences.

nodes.label: Route uncertainty to expertise
nodes.description: Contact relevant specialists when identifiable; otherwise contact a direct manager or stakeholder.

nodes.label: Respond to evidence-backed criticism
nodes.description: Generally accepts fact-backed criticism; fixes own mistakes quickly where possible, otherwise communicates and plans next steps per project setup.

nodes.label: Direct feedback with references
nodes.description: Gives feedback directly, usually with references for the recipient to explore.

nodes.label: Owner first, public visibility as last lever
nodes.description: If an interested contact exists, goes to that person first. Where no one is invested in improving the setup, sees public visibility as the only remaining option.

nodes.label: Healthy delivery and motivated peers
nodes.description: Energised when planned initiatives stay on track, customers are happy, and peers are motivated.

nodes.label: Refactoring and simplification
nodes.description: Enjoys keeping systems and code clean and to the point, in the past also beyond immediate business requirements.

nodes.label: New domains, still backend
nodes.description: Most experience is e-commerce backend; currently more interested in new fields of work while staying in backend engineering. Learning a new landscape is an accepted investment.

nodes.label: Unclear ownership and lack of follow-through
nodes.description: Strongly demotivated when ownership is unclear or responsible people do not respond after effort has been invested.

nodes.label: Money-driven over value-driven culture
nodes.description: Dislikes cultures and management focused on income rather than serving others well; prefers shared values and goals. Does not imply opposition to fair compensation.

nodes.label: Async-first, direct communication
nodes.description: Prefers open, direct, low-ceremony async communication such as Slack over finding meeting slots when async can move work forward.

nodes.label: Sync for critical events and changes
nodes.description: Prefers synchronous meetings for communicating critical events or changes.

nodes.label: Public, on-topic discussion
nodes.description: Welcomes interested people contributing publicly, provided discussions remain on topic.

nodes.label: Evidence-based disagreement
nodes.description: Wants opinions supported by arguments and facts; values willingness to recognise being wrong.

nodes.label: Aligned autonomy
nodes.description: Align on the goal and rough boundaries up front, then allow freedom to find a creative solution.

nodes.label: Delegate external organisational communication
nodes.description: Prefers managers, product owners, or similar roles to handle communication with other companies or departments.

nodes.label: High-level guidance, independent problem-solving
nodes.description: Avoids teaching topics already documented online; in unclear situations gives a high-level picture and leaves details to the learner.

nodes.label: Timely feedback
nodes.description: Believes immediate feedback is preferable to periodic feedback; has limited experience receiving it.

nodes.label: Written, inspectable decisions
nodes.description: Prefers ADRs, and arc42 records for larger-impact decisions: alternatives, criteria, trade-offs, and rationale, with weighted decision-making where appropriate. Talking without recording a decision is ineffective.

nodes.label: Idea contributor and alignment keeper
nodes.description: Brings ideas, tracks alignment, tries to reduce room for mistakes, leads by example, and learns from people with stronger expertise.

nodes.label: Java backend engineering
nodes.description: Strongest core area; 14+ years. CV lists Java 21, Kotlin, Spring Boot and Spring, concurrency, REST, AMQP, Kafka, Temporal.

nodes.label: SAP Commerce (Hybris)
nodes.description: Main platform across most roles. SAP Certified Development Professional (Commerce 6.0); author of the open-source flexiblesearchbuilder library.

nodes.label: Architecture and software quality
nodes.description: System architecture, architectural quality characteristics, software quality, and creative solutions to software-related business problems.

nodes.label: Agentic AI development practices
nodes.description: Applied over roughly the last year; reports using 'agent guides' before later-standardised terminology was announced. Evidence of initiative, not proof of expertise in every subdomain.

nodes.label: Agentic AI topics
nodes.description: Skills, commands, MCP, permissions, and headless automations.

nodes.label: Azure DevOps CI/CD
nodes.description: Pipeline work on Azure DevOps, including build-time and test-strategy improvements.

nodes.label: Cloud and observability stack, operator level
nodes.description: Uses Kubernetes, Helm, ArgoCD, Terraform, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus/Grafana and Dynatrace as an operator: application instrumentation, new metrics and dashboards, deployments. Does not set up or administer the platforms themselves (e.g. Grafana instances, data sources, clusters).

nodes.label: Observability and KPI setup
nodes.description: Strong interest in clear metrics and using them to drive direction.

nodes.label: Mentoring and small-team lead
nodes.description: Led a server-side team of 3; mentored 3 engineers through SAP Commerce certification; onboarded new team members.

nodes.label: Working languages
nodes.description: English fluent and the main work language; German B2, mostly non-work vocabulary; Ukrainian native, Russian bilingual; Italian in progress.

nodes.label: Spoken communication
nodes.description: Self-assessed as currently weak. An active improvement goal, seen as key to further career growth. Not a fixed trait.

nodes.label: Deep DevOps and infrastructure
nodes.description: Limited depth in OS internals, agent-pool management, and platform administration. Interested; will dive in when a concrete need arises.

nodes.label: Frontend and design
nodes.description: Not an expertise area; prefers to delegate to specialists.

nodes.label: Business contract negotiation
nodes.description: No prior experience; prefers to delegate, including for own contracting agreements.

nodes.label: Extensions extracted from the monorepo
nodes.description: Introduced the concept and setup to move platform-based extensions out of the monorepo with a dedicated CI build: about 10 minutes instead of about 1 hour. The decoupling benefit is real but hard to measure in the short term.

nodes.label: Change-based testing in CI
nodes.description: Average monorepo CI pipeline time reduced by about 22%.

nodes.label: Shared integration test data
nodes.description: Cut about 6 minutes per pipeline run and reduced test-authoring effort codebase-wide.

nodes.label: Agent skills adopted by 6 teams
nodes.description: Authored agent skills, commands and guardrails with pre-configured profiles, adopted by 6 teams. Context from the interview: adoption followed a hackathon that required agentic AI and happened largely because no alternative setup existed, not through a persuasion campaign.

nodes.label: Headless agent automations
nodes.description: Built headless coding-agent automations to raise coverage and repair broken tests; published the ultra-plan CLI on PyPI.

nodes.label: Internal developer tools
nodes.description: IntelliJ plugin used by 20+ developers; co-authored a deeplink browser extension used by 30+ engineering, QA and operations colleagues.

nodes.label: Payment and fulfilment integrations
nodes.description: Four payment provider integrations (Adyen, Braintree, Scalapay, Worldpay) and order-fulfilment Temporal workflows.

nodes.label: Telco identity flow under load
nodes.description: Solved concurrency and data-integrity failures in a telco identity flow (MSISDN integration and storage) under production load.

nodes.label: Attempt to establish ownership
nodes.description: Clarified target audience, tried to assign responsibility to relevant managers, and made the issue visible in an appropriate channel. Some clarifications followed, but requested sign-offs did not; stopped because there was insufficient authority to push further.

nodes.label: Public KPI audit
nodes.description: Had an agent analyse all KPI metrics, report outdated and duplicate ones, and plan next steps (alignment, connection, ownership). Shared it in a public channel; nobody replied there. The manager then called to say it was harmful and of zero value; Andrii pushed back with arguments.

nodes.label: Silence as a sign of the organisation
nodes.description: Andrii reads the lack of response as a sign of the organisation's state, and the manager's reaction as money-driven rather than value-driven management, which he strongly disrespects. The manager's own view was not captured.

nodes.label: Creates visibility to establish ownership
nodes.description: Clarify audience and problem, identify the responsible group, create visibility, then seek explicit ownership. Participation without the needed decision is not completion. May stop when authority is missing.

nodes.label: Influence through enablement
nodes.description: Influence appears strongest when providing ready-made assets that fill an existing gap, rather than negotiating buy-in. Based mainly on one adoption example.

nodes.label: Early engagement prevents public escalation
nodes.description: A collaborator who acts as the interested contact when Andrii raises systemic issues is likely to keep the discussion direct rather than public.

nodes.label: Public gap-surfacing can read as criticism
nodes.description: Surfacing organisational gaps publicly without prior alignment with the affected owner may be perceived as exposure, even when intended as a fix.

nodes.label: Value conflict may become visible
nodes.description: Strong disagreement with leadership seen as money-driven may show as low respect toward that leadership and strain the relationship.

nodes.label: Do: state values and priorities clearly
nodes.description: Make the goal, values and priorities explicit up front.

nodes.label: Do: leave room for creative solutions
nodes.description: Once direction and constraints are set, leave the how open.

nodes.label: Do: be the interested contact
nodes.description: When he raises a systemic issue, engage early and take or assign ownership.

nodes.label: Never: leave raised issues without response or owner
nodes.description: Especially after he has invested effort in clarifying the problem.

nodes.label: Never: expect many parallel streams at full quality
nodes.description: For example ten things in parallel, all completed at a good quality level.

nodes.label: Remote from Italy, CET
nodes.description: Based in Ascoli Piceno, Italy. Temporary relocation possible for specific needs.

nodes.label: Limited travel, flexible hours
nodes.description: Business trips at most once per month; flexible working hours desired.

nodes.label: Sufficient and fair compensation
nodes.description: As the main income, pay has to be sufficient and fair for the job scope.

nodes.label: Employment or contracting
nodes.description: Open to employment (including employer of record) or contracting through his own practice, hybriscraft. Available from October 2026; German citizenship, no EU work permit needed.
